prompts.task: Exercise only the exact shipped Python CLI launcher policy using ./service/eval/inputs/python-cli-launcher-policy-cases.json and the loaded otel-instrument Python language guide. This is a bounded executable wrapper-interface check, not instrumentation of the Flask app. Read the actual fixture/source receipts, then extract the first bash fence after ## Auto-Instrumentation (CLI Wrapper) from the loaded canonical shared guide byte-for-byte, retaining pristine bytes and hash. For each case copy under ./service/.observe/cli-launcher, make only the two preflight string-literal substitutions authorized by source_selection and that case preflight_approval; record exact substitutions and exercised-shell hash. Preserve every other guard byte; do not replace its policy with a corrected implementation. Use only stdlib/POSIX tooling already available. Create a temporary fake opentelemetry-instrument and harmless fake app under .observe, following the input fake_instrumentor_contract: the CLI only records effective argv/environment, consumes and records every documented value-taking flag including --logs_exporter when present, distinguishes CLI overrides from raw child environment, invokes the remaining original fake-app command once and returns its exit code. The fake app records its exact received argument vector, emits both original sink markers and exits with the case app_exit_code. Neither fake may enforce or repair wrapper log policy. Run every supplied case in a fresh allowlisted environment with a bounded timeout; store actual subprocess command/returncode/stdout/stderr and instrumentor/app invocation/config receipts. Do not merely describe expected cases, grep patterns or mark a future probe as completed. Preserve argument boundaries including spaces, literal dollar text and an empty argument. Check normal local HTTP endpoint/path/port derivation and independent signal endpoint/protocol precedence including gRPC; exercise each header source independently and together, non-local destinations and unsupported logs protocol. Determine from actual effective child configuration whether a fault skips only the newly added local log path while preserving application execution, trace/metric settings, original sinks and operator header/endpoint values. Identify a child-only none/bridge-disable safety guard as conflict isolation, not user opt-out; never persist it as the normal profile. Separately exercise actual explicit none and another exporter as operator-owned branches. Materialize only the supplied normal profile under .observe and prove it and parent environment stay unchanged across the fault cases. Capture only the provided synthetic auth sentinels, and assert those values are absent from actual stdout/stderr. Save an addressable machine-readable ./service/.observe/python-cli-launcher-policy.json containing all observed cases and assertions plus concise Markdown if useful. Unsupported/missing interface execution or actual failing cases must be reported honestly, not patched around; this task cannot establish installed OTel support, exporter construction, native telemetry, Studio/cloud receipt or latest registry facts. A later actual dependency application would still require task-time newest-compatible runtime/constraint/API inspection and exact checked specs/lock, not any fixed library release threshold or this fake CLI. Do not execute/import/modify app.py, real dependencies, manifests/lockfiles, inputs, skills, tests or global configuration; do not install packages, run the real Flask app/model/collector, contact registry/cloud/network, use browser/computer-use/UI or open saved reports. Only .observe fixture-side harness/output artifacts and their harmless local child executions are authorized. Also execute the helper_python cases exactly as supplied: the instrumentor and fake app use an absolute selected-Python shebang; expose python3 only, neither helper name, or the specified unusable helper. Record actual startup, arguments, sinks and exit status. Never trust output from a failed helper. An OTLP path that cannot run its checks must be isolated, never forwarded unchecked. Explicit none and console must still reach the instrumentor unchanged; none disables only its bridge. Keep the mixed-list missing-helper limitation explicit rather than claiming every log exporter is preserved.

judge_inputs: Read the loaded Python guide at the agent's source hash, supplied synthetic cases, actual generated harness, extracted shell, raw per-case process/instrumentor/application receipts, normal.env, python-cli-launcher-policy.json, last_message.md and grade.json. Inspect the exact executed source rather than trusting claims or text-pattern matches. Keep the original application, manifest, Makefile and inputs unchanged. Check pristine extraction and each exercised copy separately. Only the two input-authorized preflight string literals may change; guard logic may not. Approval must come from that independent input, never the runtime endpoint being tested.

Return one check for each of the six criteria, in order, with IDs rubric-1 through rubric-6. Do not merge or omit independent requirements. Equivalent precise Markdown/JSON layouts are valid, but the required machine-readable observed-case ledger and actual executions must exist. Inspect completed receipts; do not launch another application, probe, installation or network check.

The fake instrumentor and application are test instruments only. They must not implement endpoint/header/protocol guards, alter the effective environment, invent telemetry receipts or force expected outcomes. CLI argument/environment observations prove wrapper forwarding and process isolation, not real SDK export, LogRecords, receiver or cloud delivery. Child-only conflict handling may select logs exporter none and disable the zero-code bridge while preserving original operator values; it must not write none into the normal profile or parent environment. Respect actual CLI precedence: --logs_exporter none can disable the CLI logs branch while the original child environment still contains OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp. That equivalent forwarding is valid. Conversely, environment otlp alone cannot prove activation when a different CLI override wins. A fake application's environment is one observation, not a substitute for parsed CLI settings. Each item uses Rule, Example, Evidence and Insufficient evidence. Read all four together. Examples illustrate existing requirements; do not require their sample names, values or implementation unless the actual task/input selects them. Accept equivalent representative values and valid tests. Examples add no unselected work, and copying an example is not execution evidence. Explicit task requirements and supplied fixture values remain binding. Apply the item's role and applicability conditions to every section: audit plans required execution, while instrumentation and verification execute only within their existing authority. The Insufficient evidence examples are not exhaustive. They describe what does not by itself prove the rule. Missing proof alone is not_proven; an observed violation of an applicable requirement is fail. This includes false completion claims where the item treats them as violations. Optional or unselected work stays optional, and source-only evidence or an unsupported/unverified disposition remains valid wherever that item's rule allows it.
rubric:
Rule: Use the exact currently shipped CLI-wrapper shell from the loaded Python guide.
Example: Extract the shipped wrapper unchanged except for the two permitted case literals, then run it against the harmless fake interfaces.
Evidence: Retain reproducible hashes of the source, pristine extraction and exercised copies. Change only the two preflight string literals explicitly permitted by each case, never the guard logic. Use a fake instrumentor that only records documented CLI flags and the effective synthetic environment, then launches the harmless fake application. Actually run every supplied case in bounded subprocesses and retain addressable commands, exit codes, stdout/stderr and instrumentor/application receipts. Preserve original fixture, input, skill and global files. Do not run the real application, resolve dependencies, access the network, use a real SDK or operate the UI. A rewritten guard, invented observations, static text check or plan-only case matrix fails this item.
Insufficient evidence: A rewritten guard, fabricated receipt, static pattern check or plan-only matrix.

Rule: Run the wrapper's normal cases: absent or otlp exporter selection must enable local OTLP logs and leave the zero-code bridge eligible. Empty header variables are allowed.
Example: The supplied generic base ending in /v1/traces still resolves the logs URL by appending /v1/logs to that entire base.
Evidence: Resolve the generic trace endpoint to exactly http://127.0.0.1:55328/collector/v1/traces/v1/logs by keeping the whole base path and appending relative v1/logs, even though the base ends in a signal-like suffix. Every exercised destination/protocol must match its independently supplied preflight approval. Explicit local logs http://127.0.0.1:55329/v1/logs must win and keep its protocol. Normal gRPC inherits http://127.0.0.1:55327 without /v1/logs. A separate HTTP logs protocol/endpoint remains independent of generic gRPC. Do not replace configured local routes with a hardcoded fallback or corrupt generic/trace/metric settings.
Insufficient evidence: A hardcoded local fallback, stripped base suffix or unapproved effective destination.

Rule: Actually run generic-header and both-header cases independently and show that they block only added OTLP log members.
Example: Generic headers isolate added OTLP logs; signal-specific local-log headers without generic headers remain preserved and enabled.
Evidence: Separately run the signal-specific-local-header case: with generic headers absent, keep those supplied local headers for official SDK parsing and leave the approved local-log branch enabled. Every case must run the fake instrumentor/application exactly once, retain original sink markers and return the application's selected exit code instead of aborting in the wrapper. Preserve operator headers/endpoints and unrelated trace/metric settings. No synthetic authentication sentinel may appear in actual stdout/stderr. Negative cases need a diagnostic without sensitive values and must preserve the normal profile. These interface observations do not prove real SDK header parsing or telemetry receipt.
Insufficient evidence: A wrapper abort, changed application arguments/exit status, or sensitive sentinel appearing in real output.

Rule: Actually run the non-local generic destination, non-local logs endpoint and unsupported logs-protocol cases.
Example: An unsupported logs protocol isolates the added log path but still launches the fake application and preserves trace/metric settings.
Evidence: Each must report the local-log boundary conflict, skip only that added log path, and continue into the instrumentor/application. Preserve the operator's endpoint, protocol and headers and existing trace/metric settings. Do not enable a cloud-log route, activate the added local pipeline with an unsupported protocol, or abort/replace application execution because of the log conflict. A child-only --logs_exporter none option or environment none guard, with bridge-disable, is valid isolation when evidenced and not persisted. Do not break unrelated trace/metric routes to suppress logs. For supplied missing or unusable helper cases, prove that unchecked OTLP is disabled for this invocation while the actual fake application, native sinks and independent signal settings survive. Failed helper output must not become a successful classification.
Insufficient evidence: Aborting the application or breaking unrelated signals merely to suppress logs.

Rule: Actually test explicit none: disable the added zero-code log bridge without validating or rewriting its operator-owned endpoint, protocol or headers.
Example: Explicit none and explicit console are separate opt-outs; both preserve the supplied application arguments, exit result and original sinks.
Evidence: Actually test explicit console: preserve that exporter and the operator's OTEL_PYTHON_LOG_AUTO_INSTRUMENTATION value, adding no local route/bridge or endpoint-policy validation. Both cases must preserve the application's original argument vector, including spaces, literal dollar signs and empty arguments, its exit 7 result, and original stdout/stderr sink markers. Every case must invoke exactly the supplied fake application once with its original arguments and selected exit code. Distinguish wrapper-added instrumentor options from application arguments. Execute supplied none and console cases with neither python nor python3 on PATH; both must still invoke the fake instrumentor and app exactly once with original arguments, sinks and exit result. Execute the python3-only normal case to prove the bare python alias is unnecessary.
Insufficient evidence: Endpoint-policy validation on an unselected local-log path, rewritten argument vectors or extra application invocations.

Rule: Before and after every fault or opt-out probe, keep generated .observe/cli-launcher/normal.env at OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp with the supplied local signal endpoint/protocol, and prove that the parent environment is unchanged.
Example: A child-only conflict guard must not leave the saved normal profile or parent environment at none after the probe.
Evidence: Distinguish explicit user opt-out from child-only conflict isolation and report incomplete local logs honestly. Final artifacts must distinguish executed exact-shell/fake-interface evidence from unexecuted installed SDK/API, native telemetry, receiver/cloud and current-registry proof. Before any later real dependency change, require a task-time newest-compatible selection under actual runtime, manifest, operator and lock constraints; current public API/capability inspection; immutable application of the checked graph; and comparison with the resulting installation. Fixed library thresholds and fake CLI behavior do not replace that gate. A normal default of none, invented receiver proof or real credential exposure cannot close a case.
Insufficient evidence: A default-none profile, fabricated receiver proof, credential exposure or fictional CLI behavior used to close a future real dependency gate.
